/assets/ping/media/6954e5dcd0ebbca07d234.alt: Three research columns with photographs of families and children using devices. Panel text: Why do families give their kids mobile devices? Families want to stay connected Parents need reliable ways to reach their children and ensure their safety during emergencies. Mobile devices provide this essential connection. Smart devices solve parents worries Modern devices include safety tools, location sharing, and communication features that address parents' core concerns about their children's wellbeing. Parent anxiety outweighs device misuse concerns Parents know smart devices expose kids to apps, distractions, and online risks. But the fear of being unable to reach their child is more tangible, justifying a trade-off.

/assets/niche/media/689b243727ef1fe97436.alt: Three office photographs with desk research captions about meetings and workplace space. Panel text: Desk Research Video conferences surged nearly 30x during the peak of COVID Since then, virtual meetings have stabilized at 250% above pre-COVID levels, making virtual meetings a normal part of the workday. Many companies are enforcing return-to-office mandates, hoping to boost productivity Half of Fortune 100 companies now require employees to work onsite, a sharp increase from just 5% in 2023. Office layouts were not designed for this change in meeting culture, creating more demand than space allows Over half of workers describe their workplace as noisy, and even more say there aren't enough spaces for private, solo calls. Sources: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/great-expectations-making-hybrid-work-work, https://kpmg.com/xx/en/our-insights/value-creation/kpmg-global-ceo-outlook-survey-2024.html

As sustainable materials grow in demand, the mycelium name is frequently thrown around. However, when first introduced to people, it unfamiliar and confusing. The Hyphae light seeks to change that by telling the story through form.
Deriving its form from the microscopic growth patterns of mycelium, the shape and material of the Hyphae light introduce viewers to the material through sculptural expression of its growth.

Mycelium is the white root system found living in the ground beneath mushrooms. When grown in wood chips, mycelium becomes a material somewhere between styrofoam and MDF, but 100% compostable. The composites sustainability and structure is what has made the design community excited about it.

/assets/hyphae/media/673e515a8fcf893cc96.alt: Text panel describing hyphae and the project goal. Panel text: Hyphae, the building blocks of mycelium Mycelium is made up of of hyphae, exploring limbs in search of nutrients. Invisibly small, they become apparent to the eye as a mass of white veins after thousands of searching strands overlap. Mycelium is alien on first encounter. It's a spongy membrane of velvety white material, spotted with stains of what look like mold growth. Introducing its to a consumer landscape made of plastics and metals is confusing. By telling the story of hyphae growth through sculpture, I hope to familiarize consumers with this future material. This projects goal is to introduce mycelium material to consumers.

/assets/hyphae/media/673e516f3a016af805e.alt: Text panel describing the transition from growth simulation to sculptural form. Panel text: Extracting form from nature To tell the story of mycelium, I wanted to reveal the microscopic growth patterns to consumers. There is beauty in the growth that I felt viewer would resonate with, if it could be shown at a larger scale. My plan was to extract the shape from early growth stages, turn that into a 3d model, and make that into a sculptural lighting fixture. By using Mycologist David Moore's cyberfungi algorithm, which simulates accurate mycelium growth, I was able to create a true to nature digital model. From that digital growth model, I extracted a set of lines which I translated into a 3D model.
/assets/hyphae/media/673e516f3a016af805e.heading: Extracting form from nature

Panel text: Making the skeleton To make my digital model into a real mycelium-coated prototype, I split the shape up into parts which I could CNC, then glue together. Wood would allow the mycelium root-structure to grow into the skeleton material, creating strength.
/assets/hyphae/media/673e51809aa0efa0f07.heading: Making the skeleton

blocks.text: To make my digital model into a real mycelium-coated prototype, I split the shape up into parts which I could CNC, then glue together. Wood would allow the mycelium root-structure to grow into the skeleton material, creating strength.

/assets/hyphae/media/673e5189dca399c9dc4.alt: Photographs of the branching skeleton wrapped with substrate and the exposed growth.

/assets/hyphae/media/673e5191244aba7f345.alt: Text panel describing the mycelium growing process. Panel text: Growing mycelium I surrounded the skeleton with living mycelium composite, and used saran wrap to secure the loose chips. Then, I covered the model in clay, poked holes, and hydrated it. That convinces the living material that it is underground and gets it to grow. After five days, I unwrapped the prototype to reveal healthy mycelium growth. Hyphae can be seen growing within the wooden skeleton.
/assets/hyphae/media/673e5191244aba7f345.heading: Growing mycelium

blocks.text: I surrounded the skeleton with living mycelium composite, and used saran wrap to secure the loose chips. Then, I covered the model in clay, poked holes, and hydrated it. That convinces the living material that it is underground and gets it to grow.

/assets/hyphae/media/673e51f924ce4848d12.alt: Closing text panel describing possible further iterations. Panel text: Next steps Though the model was executed effectively, considering its 2 week production period, it leaves a lot to be desired. In further iterations, I would primarily focus on production methods and also implement a more realistic lighting system. I would explore using a latex mold to grow the mycelium. That would allow me to better define limits of the growth and a less intense skeleton. I also plan on exploring an internal lighting harness, allowing power from one source to route to lights on each end.
